\begin{abstract}
LLM judges are widely deployed for evaluation and alignment, yet style features alone explain judge scores with near-perfect correlation.
We introduce Controlled Style Decomposition (CSD), a black-box framework that detects per-axis style bias through style-controlled rewriting, NLI content gating, and pairwise comparison.

A third judge (Claude Sonnet 4) detects no bias on either axis, confirming discriminative validity.
Style bias audits require pairwise comparison; existing Likert-based null findings may reflect measurement insensitivity rather than genuine absence of bias.
